versions.changelog:
Moonbase 2.4.0 is the server side of Moonfin 2.7.0. It builds the new seasonal Home row, gives custom rows each title's rating and holds them to parental limits, gets large MDBList rows loading, and matches anime with non-English library titles. It also syncs the settings the new clients added and bundles the Moonfin 2.7.0 web app.

Features:

- A seasonal Home row of holiday movies a user owns, plus Seerr suggestions, for New Year's, Valentine's Day, Easter, Pride, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas, Lunar New Year and Diwali. Clients turn it on, and a new Moonfin Seasonal Keywords Sync task fills in TMDB keywords using the server-wide TMDB key.
- Custom row items carry the TMDB certification, overview, genres and runtime, and rows fetched with a user's own TMDB or MDBList key are cached for that user.
- The bottom bar style and tabs, the Friends button, detail screen sections and seasonal effect density now sync, with admin defaults for the bottom bar, the Friends button, the new seasonal effects, density, the seasonal row and the Great-Grandparents interface size.
- The bundled web app moves up to Moonfin 2.7.0, with friends and chat from the Achievement Badges plugin, the seasonal row and new seasonal effects, a remote control D-pad, Live TV recovery, Library Order and detail screen sections.

Bug Fixes:

- Anime markers match series whose library title isn't English or romaji.
- New request notifications reach every Seerr request manager by default.
- Large MDBList rows load, since the server keeps resolving them after the app gives up.
- TMDB TV chart rows open the right show instead of a movie with the same id.
- Custom rows respect each user's parental limit. Set a server-wide TMDB key, or limited users get empty MDBList, IMDb and Letterboxd rows.
- Jellyfin Enhanced's header buttons stop opening Moonfin Web.
- In the web app, Seerr notifications reach the browser, Seerr rows load without an eight second wait after sign-in, subtitles set to Off stay off, and home rows stop going blank on Firefox.

Moonbase 2.3.0 adds the backend for anime markers, scores recommendations on the server, and keeps a backup of its settings with a restore button. It fixes message text that could wipe every plugin setting on a restart, gets the scheduled tasks running on their own again on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12, and bundles the Moonfin 2.6.0 web app.

Features:

- Anime markers flag filler, mixed, canon and recap episodes using the Anime Filler List and Tenrai, and mark Subbed or Dubbed from the audio in your own files. It's off by default, under Integrations.
- Recommendations are scored on the server. On Jellyfin 12 that scoring plugs into Jellyfin's own similar items so every client gets it, and a switch under Integrations hands it back to Jellyfin.
- Moonbase keeps a backup of its server settings and offers to restore it if they ever come back reset.
- Clients can show when a series airs next through the server, even without Sonarr.
- Admin defaults for the metadata row, the loading animation, the screensaver, the new detail screen styles, Seerr missing collection items and availability badges, the Downloads and Live TV buttons, the Rate action button, fallback audio and subtitle languages, and the Grandparents interface size.
- The bundled web app moves up to Moonfin 2.6.0, with the Spotlight, Nouveau and Minimalist detail screens, Kids Mode, Achievement Badges, a redone Live TV guide, and fonts that no longer load from Google.

Bug Fixes:

- Message text can no longer corrupt the settings file, which Jellyfin answered by resetting every setting and sometimes removing the plugin on the next start.
- Applying defaults only changes what the admin actually set.
- Scheduled tasks run on their own on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12, and custom home rows now refresh daily.
- Notifications, the media bar and genre lists stop showing items a user isn't allowed to see.
- Hidden Continue Watching and Next Up items stay hidden on every device.
- Retro game artwork is far more reliable on large libraries, and PSP games can start in Moonfin Web once the new isolation checkbox under Retro Games is on.
- The Moonfin header button shows in the Jellyfin 12 web UI.

Moonbase 2.2.0 adds server messages, so an admin can write something once and have it show up in people's apps even when they were offline while it was sent. The admin defaults page grows a lot, with settings for another 96 options and fixes to the six controls that were writing values no client reads. Retro games find more of their artwork, and it now picks up new ROMs without a restart. A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out, and a zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The bundled web client moves up to Moonfin 2.5.1.

Features:

- A new Messages tab lets an admin write a message with a title and a Markdown body, pick a colour, choose how it shows up, pick who sees it, schedule a start and end date, add a link button, and order the list. Broadcast now saves what it sends, so a user who was offline still finds it.
- Admin defaults picked up settings for another 96 options, covering discovery rows, Since You Watched, music rows, sort direction for the home rows, player buttons, media segments, Cinema Mode for episodes, and a lot more.
- Six admin controls that were writing values no client reads now send the right ones, and row sorting was rebuilt to match the clients, which also adds the missing Playlist Order option.
- Retro games now watch the configured game library folders for file changes, so a new ROM or a per-library scan runs artwork reconciliation in the background instead of waiting for a restart, and games that came out as a false miss are retried once the matching has corrected them.
- The settings sync toggle was renamed to Moonbase Sync, and its description now says that enabling it is required for the Seerr and ratings integrations.
- The bundled web client picks up everything web relevant from Moonfin 2.5.1, including the messages window, a Seerr poster grid with a download progress bar, remote subtitle badges, Play and Resume on the long press menu, and personal ratings writing to Emby.

Bug Fixes:

- A reinstalled Seerr no longer strands you logged out. The plugin was reading every 403 as missing admin rights, so the stale session was never cleared. Now it checks whether Seerr still knows the session first, and a definite refusal clears the old session and signs in again.
- A zipped game now arrives as the ROM it actually is. The detail was naming the archive, so a client saved plain ROM bytes under a .zip name and failed to unpack them. It now names the file the endpoint actually sends, along with its real size.
- A pending artwork timer can no longer take the process down on shutdown, and the artwork delivery route rejects an unknown role instead of falling through.
- The websocket reconnects after a server restart, a busy server no longer reads as a connection timeout, and Escape closes the dialog on top instead of the page behind it.

Moonbase 2.1.0 is mostly about the retro games backend, plus a personal ratings API, audiobook bookmark sync, and the bundled Moonfin web app at 2.5.0.

Features:

- Retro games: arcade ZIPs are validated offline against FBNeo and MAME DAT files, and admins can upload a DAT per core through the plugin.
- Retro games: ROMs are identified by their contents through the libretro RDB databases, with per game core and backend overrides.
- Retro games: a server side artwork pipeline with a manifest, per game artwork priority, and cached thumbnails at the requested size and format. Reconciliation runs on plugin startup and after every library scan.
- Retro games: delivery and per user concurrency limiters, a real Moonfin bridge for the EmulatorJS web player, and archive hashing capped at 512 MB per entry.
- A personal ratings endpoint serves the calling user's ratings in one response, so clients can sort and filter libraries by them.
- Audiobook bookmarks and notes are stored on the server and synced between clients.
- Clients can read their own transcode jobs, so transcoded downloads show real progress and an ETA.
- Settings sync covers everything Moonfin 2.5.0 added: HDR subtitle style, per segment skip actions, home row sort orders, the Studios row, spoiler free toggles, personal rating style, media type badges, segment auto hide, swipe gestures, scroll sensitivity, Cinema Mode for episodes, external trailers, and the crash report toggle.
- Admin defaults page: home row toggles with per row sorting defaults, Seerr Watchlist and Seerr shortcuts rows, the Aya media bar style, a Recently Released series type default, and pushing a genre, collection, or playlist row now enables its category toggle.
- The plugin reports itself as Moonbase throughout the dashboard.

Bug Fixes:

- TV studios get their logos, since TMDB networks are now read alongside production companies. Network ids are namespaced apart from company ids and the logo cache index is versioned.
- Seerr provisioning reports why it stopped instead of a bare status.
- IMDb charts stopped returning 403.
- Admin defaults: browsing and details blur defaults no longer fail the whole save, the theme music volume default is saved, and the Continue Watching image type options send values the client understands.

Web App:

- Bundles Moonfin 2.5.0 with the first run setup wizard, the Aya media bar, the full set of library sorts and filters, personal ratings, Seerr browse shortcuts, a Live TV favorites row, a Studio row, Live TV series recording, spoiler free toggles, an expanded metadata editor, Vim style playback keys, per segment skip actions, an HDR subtitle style, and crash reports sent to your own server.
- Fixes for playback control flicker, the skip button, subtitle offset range, Seerr row hover and localization, Continue Watching and Next Up paging, library search with Group By, blurry search posters, context menu placement, studio logo matching, media bar gradient flashing, backdrop fades, source pickers losing ids, book summaries, right to left layouts, and internationalized server domain names.

Features:

- Added a Playback tab to the admin defaults page, covering autoplay, audio and subtitle language, subtitle mode, skip lengths, intro action, still watching behavior, Next Up timeout, and rewind durations.
- Added default pickers for Action Buttons and Seerr Discovery row order.
- Added profile properties for OLED mode, the player time labels, and the new home row options, so those settings sync between devices.
- Game ROM and BIOS routes answer HEAD requests, which is how clients check a file's size before downloading it.

Bug Fixes:

- The Playback admin tab now writes the keys, values, and units clients actually read. Several pickers were saving under names no client looked for, so those defaults silently did nothing.
- Resume Rewind and Unpause Rewind options match what the client offers, instead of listing durations it has no setting for.
- Removed admin controls that no longer map to anything a client syncs. The underlying profile properties stay in place, so device to device sync is unaffected.
- Fixed the label text on the Details Screen Blur setting.

Features:

- Push notifications now reach Moonfin apps even when they're closed, covering Seerr activity, new media added to your library, and admin broadcasts. Admins can point at a self-hosted relay or their own FCM service account.
- Custom home rows sync across device profiles, so a row you build on one device shows up on the others, and edits and deletions carry over.
- Added a Max Days in Next Up setting.
- MDBList gained a Test Key button that shows your plan and remaining quota, a Clear Cache button, a max items limit for official lists, and Roger Ebert as a rating source.
- Added button layout sync so clients keep their player and details button layouts per device type.
- Glass and 8-bit Hero joined the admin default theme picker, along with the 8-bit Gold accent.

Bug Fixes:

- Fixed MDBList rows dropping shows, since the item cap was applied unevenly across the separate movie and show lists.
- Fixed Rotten Tomatoes critic scores never matching.
- MDBList rate limits are handled properly now, with your quota checked before syncing and partial results kept instead of overwriting good cached data.
- Ratings are filtered by the requesting device's profile instead of always using the global one.
- Fixed the Ping response casing that made clients report Seerr as not configured, and Emby media bar items now come back in the shape clients expect.
- Fixed the Emby plugin settings page never loading.
- Cancelling a Seerr request you don't have permission to cancel no longer logs you out of Seerr.
- The settings updated broadcast only fires when a save actually changed something, which stops sync loops between devices.
- Fixed the Seerr media available webhook breaking on some Jellyfin versions.

Features:

- Added password-less Seerr sign in through a Quick Connect bridge, so users who log in with Quick Connect get signed into Seerr silently.
- Added a server-side Radarr and Sonarr calendar proxy so clients can show upcoming release calendars, reachable for non-admin accounts too.
- Widened settings sync from 87 synced settings to 207, backed by new settings profile properties.
- Hardened game metadata matching with accent normalization and fuzzy suffix matching for better ROM artwork and details.
- On Emby, Moonfin web assets are now served with an explicit content type so the frontend loads correctly.
- The bundled Moonfin Web client moves up to the latest codebase, bringing a music overhaul with a Songs sublibrary and shuffle controls, a rebuilt downloads engine, a retro games library browser, Emby Skip Intro via chapter markers, and new detail and media bar controls.

Bug Fixes:

- Fixed the Rotten Tomatoes critics rating mismatch coming from MDBList.
- Fixed Seerr sessions being evicted on 403 Forbidden responses, and stopped a failed auto-login leaving Seerr stuck as unavailable.
- Many bundled web fixes across music resume, subtitles, multi-server library browse, the media bar, Seerr requests, and focus handling.

Features:

- Moonbase now runs on Emby servers in addition to Jellyfin, bringing settings sync, the Seerr proxy, custom rows, and the rest of the plugin's backend to Emby.
- The bundled Moonfin Web client was rebuilt from the latest codebase, picking up the Modern details screen, fully custom home rows with external sources, the Seerr overhaul with SSO through the plugin, a full admin panel makeover, TV Mode on web, the Theme Store and new themes, music and book updates, and user scoped settings.

## Features

- Fix the banner covering the top navigation on Jellyfin 12.0's new "modern" UI. JellyFlare now detects the layout and pushes the nav bar and content down instead of drawing over them. 10.11 and TV unchanged. (fixes #12)

**Jellyfin 12.0:** you don't need the File Transformation plugin. JavaScript Injector injects the banner on its own. If you kept File Transformation from 10.11, remove it: its current build isn't 12.0-compatible and, while installed, stops the banner from injecting.

Thanks to @nothing2obvi for the report and for confirming the File Transformation behaviour on 12.0. ❤️

- Add per-banner link popup hint: each rotation message and permanent entry can now carry its own optional hint text shown above the Open/Copy/Cancel buttons, overriding the global default. Per-banner hint → global default → nothing (when both empty). Existing setups keep working unchanged. The Settings-tab field is relabeled "Default link popup hint" to reflect the fallback (requested by @nerdc0re-net #9)

- Fix maintenance mode error 500 on Jellyfin 10.11.10: `IUserManager.Users` was removed and replaced by `GetUsers()`; the plugin now compiles against the 10.11.10 SDK so the call resolves correctly (thanks @LRoffic for the report — #11)
- Bump minimum supported Jellyfin version to 10.11.10 (users on 10.11.6-10.11.9 could stay on v1.15.1 until they update Jellyfin)

- Fix banner not showing on Jellyfin instances configured with a base URL (e.g. `/jellyfin`); plugin fetches now go through `ApiClient.getUrl()` so the base URL is honored (thanks @Kayoku and @FazeThree71 for the report — #10)
- Add Monthly schedule type for banners: target the nth weekday of every month (e.g. "second Tuesday", "last Friday"), with an optional time window

- Add per-user banner muting: users can hide the rotating and/or permanent banner for their own account from their Jellyfin Display settings
- Per-account preference syncs across devices and live across open tabs; maintenance mode is never affected
- Add admin master switch to allow/forbid user muting, plus a configurable warning text (Settings tab)

- Add limit on link preview size
- Add option for comment on link popup

- Fix copy and open link in Jellyfin Media Player on desktop not working
- Update CI to avoid overwriting releases

- Add route filtering on each banner
- Add new project status in the README: project stays active but has reach a satisfying state and stays opens to bug report and feature requests but will not be as proactive as in its early development

- Add scheduling for maintenance mode and restart
- Improve UX for maintenance tab
- Add documentation link to the config page
- Add dependency warning on the config page as a warning banner

- (Tested, but use it with caution) Add a maintenance tab to let you work on your instance without user connecting to the server
- Add preview of affected users (maintenance)
- Add a reset button (maintenance) and link it to the global reset button
- Adjust dismiss button font sizes based on config settings
- Fixed close button visibility logic based on config

- Fixed the "hide all" configuration not being effective
- Added issue templates

Important changes:

- Update manifest description
- Add refresh prompt on each save
- Improve reset mechanism clarity with three distinct buttons and updated labels alongside alerts to save the config
- Improve alert rendering on misconfiguration on input validation
- Regroup isolated settings into Behavior category
- Dismissing a message, all messages, or the permanent banner now syncs instantly to other open tabs via a BroadcastChannel.
- Remove or update legacy code from first implementation

Various refactoring, safety and robustness fixes detailed below:

- `TextAlign` and `TransitionSpeed` are now whitelisted on save; invalid values normalise to `"center"` / `"normal"` rather than being stored verbatim.
- `parseInt` calls in `checkTimeWindow` now always pass radix `10`, preventing silent misparses on malformed time strings.
- Invalid-date checks for fixed schedules use `isNaN(date.getTime())` instead of `isNaN(date)` for clarity.
- `closeBtn.innerHTML` replaced with `closeBtn.textContent` for consistency with the rest of the codebase.
- Token retrieval deduplicated into a single `getToken()` helper used at both call sites.
- French tooltip text on the close and dismiss-all buttons replaced with English equivalents.
- Fixed a 50 ms race where the rotation timer could fire `tick()` before the navigation debounce resolved. The timer is now cleared immediately at the top of `onNavigate()` when `showInDashboard` is `false`.
- Plugin startup now gives up after a fixed retry count instead of looping indefinitely.
- Save endpoint rejects dangerous URL schemes (`javascript:` etc.) in both rotation and permanent entries.
- Save endpoint validates schedule types and returns a clear error for unknown values instead of silently defaulting to "always".
- Numeric settings (durations, banner height, active index) are clamped to their allowed ranges on save.
- Config changes are picked up on the next page navigation instead of waiting for the old rotation queue to finish.
- Layout recalculation now batches all reads before all writes, avoiding repeated forced reflows.
- Resize observer on the header is re-attached on every banner show, preventing stale references from rapid hide/show cycles.
- Rotation-message and permanent-entry row builders (~460 lines of duplicated code) replaced with a single shared factory function.
- Default presets, rotation messages, and permanent entries consolidated into one `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` object.
- Each Settings subsection (Appearance, Timing, Controls, Behaviour, Presets) has its own reset function; Reset and Wipe buttons delegate to these.
- Row-field collection extracted into a single shared helper used by both collect functions.
- Default text colour normalised to `#ffffff` in the data model for both rotation and permanent entries.
- Magic numbers in the banner script replaced with named constants (`BANNER_Z_INDEX`, `POPUP_Z_INDEX`, `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT`, etc.).
- Add drag and drop feature to messages collections
- Permanent banner can now optionally be dismissed, persistence behavior can be configured
- The app now tries to open link outside the in-app web browser framework, but for unsupported platform also let the user copy the url (better transparency)

- Fixed banner animation hiding first carousel arrows and title
- Added new default rotation entry
- Banner in dashboard visibility defaults to false and is set at the bottom of the config page
- Normalise line endings to inside jq before the value touches the shell

- Improved admin dashboard detection, add warning for the visibility option
- Fixed XSS vector: banner link URLs are now validated against an allowlist (https://, http://, /); any other scheme including javascript: is silently rejected
- Fixed privilege escalation: the config save endpoint (POST /JellyFlare/config) now requires admin-level credentials (RequiresElevation policy); standard user tokens are rejected
- Config and script endpoints now require authentication; unauthenticated visitors receive no banner and cannot read plugin configuration: the plugin is intended for registered users only, consistent with JS Injector
- CI actions pinned to full commit SHAs to eliminate supply-chain risk from re-tagged upstream actions
- change permanent docs image.

- add configurable sizes for dismiss buttons in settings;
- add option to show banner in admin dashboard.

- permanent banner can be disabled but still saved;
- add customization to hide all button and close button.
- add quick access to the plugin from the dashboard sidebar
- first version, may be unstable

versions.changelog: Jellyfin 12 support. This build targets Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1 (.NET 10). Servers still on 10.11 stay on the 0.10 line, which remains in this repository and keeps being offered to them - a 10.11 server will not be offered this build, and it would not load there. Nearly everything carried over unchanged. The one part of the plugin that used an API Jellyfin 12 changed is "Add as alternate version", which now links versions by item id rather than by file path, as 12 requires. On 12 that output policy also no longer waits five minutes and then warns that the merge was skipped: Jellyfin 12 recognises the companion file as a version of the source from its name, so the plugin now sees that the grouping is already in place and says so instead (issue #15). Includes the container crop fix from 0.10.1.0 (issue #14). If you are on 12 with 0.10.x installed: it does load there, but its alternate-version merge fails on 12 and is logged as a warning - updating to this release fixes that.

Fixes correct encodes being thrown away after they had finished (issue #14). A Matroska file can ask for its picture to be cropped in the container rather than in the video stream - common on UHD remuxes, where 280 lines off the top and bottom turn a 16:9 frame into a 2.40:1 film. ffmpeg 7.1 and later, including the one bundled with Jellyfin 10.11, applies that crop by itself, so the encode came out right; but the check that runs before an output is kept compared it against the uncropped size, decided the shape was wrong, and discarded the file - after however many hours the encode had taken, and on every file carrying this metadata. The crop is now read from the source, and the check accepts the picture as it is displayed as well as the uncropped frame, because an older ffmpeg ignores the crop and produces the uncropped one. It still rejects what it exists to catch: embedded cover art encoded in place of the film. The displayed size is now used everywhere else it matters too: a cropped file that already fits a resolution cap is no longer queued for nothing, the VideoWidth and VideoHeight rule conditions describe the picture you actually see, and a resolution cap no longer enlarges a cropped picture to reach a limit it was already under. Files without crop metadata - nearly all of them - behave exactly as before.

Two requested features. A daily processing window (issue #7): set "start processing at" and "pause processing at" in 30-minute steps and transcoding is confined to those hours, so a download that lands at 19:00 no longer starts encoding while you are using the machine. Outside the window nothing new is claimed and a running encode is frozen exactly where it is at the OS level - no CPU used, no progress lost - while items are still evaluated and queued, so the queue simply drains when the window opens. A stop time earlier than the start is an over-midnight window (22:00 to 06:00); equal times mean all day, so ticking the box before choosing times cannot stop the queue for ever. Times are the server's own local time, like Jellyfin's scheduled tasks. The control center now explains an automatic pause rather than just looking idle: it names the window and the time processing resumes, and the job list greys a frozen encode the way a manual pause already did. "Resume queue" outside the window asks for confirmation and then runs until the window's next edge, after which the schedule takes over again. A manual pause still overrides everything and still survives a restart. The single-item search now matches file names (issue #8): every word you type is matched against both the item's label and its full file path, so a show name, an S03E06, a 1080p or a release-group tag finds the file - alone or in combination. Typing a series name lists its episodes, grouped and in season/episode order, which was impossible before because Jellyfin's own search only ever compares an item's own name - for an episode that is the episode title, not the show, and never the path. Results are capped at 100, with a line saying how many matched in total.

Fixes a muxer error that killed jobs outright, adds hardware decoding, and fixes the queue's Pause on macOS. Audio is now negotiated against the output container the way subtitles already were: a track the container has no tag for is re-encoded instead of copied. Copying an mkv source's TrueHD track into mp4, or an aac track into webm, made the muxer reject the output header, so the whole encode died within seconds of starting - on every attempt, until the job hit the failed-attempt limit. Copy still means copy wherever the container allows it, which is all of Matroska and the common case for mp4, so profiles that already worked emit exactly the same command as before. A profile whose target audio codec the container cannot hold falls back to one it can. New "Hardware decoding" option (General): ffmpeg can decode the source on the GPU instead of the CPU, which is a large share of the work on 4K HEVC material and is worthwhile even when you encode in software. The list is built from what your own ffmpeg reports. It is off by default, because that list says what the binary was built with rather than what this machine can actually open - a method the host cannot open makes every job fail, so change it, run one job and check the queue page before leaving it on. Pausing the queue on macOS wedged the worker: the encode was suspended but the call never returned, leaving a stopped ffmpeg that nothing could resume, cancel or kill. The signal is now sent directly rather than by running /bin/kill. Also: the end-to-end test suite no longer skips itself silently on machines whose ffmpeg is not in one of three hardcoded locations, and a write-only field is no longer serialised into every queue-file write.

Splits the queue page into a control center and a paged job list, fixes issue #5, and closes a long list of defects found by a full audit. The plugin page used to fetch every job every two seconds and render a row for each one, which on a large library meant megabytes per poll and a table hundreds of screens long. The main page is now a control center - the counts, what is encoding with its progress and ETA, the next few jobs and the last few finished - with the full queue and history behind their own paged, searchable page. Issue #5: replacing a file in place with a different container renames it (Movie.mp4 to Movie.mkv) and left Jellyfin's database pointing at the deleted path, so playback failed with a file-not-found error until some later library scan; the item is now repointed at the new file, its container and size corrected, and its media info re-probed. Data safety: ffmpeg could encode embedded cover art instead of the film, and because verification only compared duration - which the audio track satisfies on its own - the original was then deleted for it under Replace in place; the stream map now excludes attached pictures and verification also checks the output's shape and audio tracks. Pausing could freeze an encode with nothing left to resume it. A clean restart no longer records a running encode as a user cancellation, waits for encodes to stop instead of orphaning ffmpeg, and sweeps the part-finished temp files that every cancel and crash used to leave behind for good. Rules: Container conditions are matched against what ffprobe actually reports, so "Container Equals mkv" matches an mkv and "NotEquals mp4" no longer matches every mp4; AudioCodec and AudioChannels are answered over every audio track instead of only the first, so a remux whose commentary is muxed ahead of the main track is no longer skipped; -preset is only passed to encoders that accept it; an image subtitle Matroska cannot store no longer aborts the encode; and an admin's own -vf is merged with the plugin's instead of being silently discarded. Also: queue writes are batched, so a sweep no longer rewrites a multi-megabyte file once per queued item, and "Cancel all" no longer does the same per cancelled job.

Answers issue #4 with a debug switch, and fixes four defects that switch made visible. New "Explain every decision in the log" option (General): each item logs what ffprobe found, every trigger-rule condition with its configured value, the value it was compared against and whether it passed, and the reason anything was skipped - so a rule that does not fire can finally be diagnosed. Fixes: a matched rule is no longer silently vetoed by the compliance check, which never looked at file size or bitrate (profiles that re-encode material already in the target codec can now switch off "Skip files already matching this profile"); a profile that would write its output over its own source is refused instead of dropping "Movie (1).mkv" beside it and re-encoding that copy on every sweep; a 10-bit source keeps its bit depth when the chosen encoder supports it, and HDR is no longer forced to 8-bit while keeping its HDR tags; and duration-based rules no longer die silently on files whose container reports no format-level duration. Also: a non-media file fails with a clear message instead of a raw ffmpeg error, an alternate version Jellyfin already grouped by filename is no longer listed twice in the version picker, the paused state survives a restart, and the finished-job history can be capped.

Two requested features. Profiles gain a "Keep original if the transcode is not smaller" option: after an encode is verified, if the new file is not smaller than the source it is discarded and your original is kept untouched — useful when re-encoding to a more efficient codec that can still produce a bigger file on some content, with no manual per-file size comparison across the library. The source is then remembered as handled, so the automatic sweep does not re-encode it on every run. Also adds a new VideoDurationMinutes trigger-rule condition, so a file-size threshold can be scaled by video length instead of a single blanket size — e.g. "duration under 30 min AND size over 350 MB".

Adds on-demand single-item pre-transcoding. From the Queue & status page there is now a "Transcode a single item" panel: search for a movie or episode by name, pick an encoding profile, and queue just that one — independent of the trigger rules and the automatic sweep (it is still skipped at run time if the item is already compliant). Also fixes the queue list appearing frozen during a slow (e.g. 4K) encode: the progress bar, elapsed time and estimated time remaining now keep updating while a job runs, instead of only redrawing when the whole-number percent changed.

A broad correctness, safety and performance release from a full code audit. Audio: the channel cap now actually downmixes (e.g. 5.1 to stereo) — it was silently ignored, which under replace-in-place also re-transcoded the file endlessly. Subtitles: mp4/mov outputs keep their text subtitles (as mov_text) instead of dropping them, and webm drops only the image subtitles it cannot store rather than failing the encode. Resolution: an odd cap (e.g. 1281) no longer aborts the encode. Encoders: VAAPI/VideoToolbox no longer receive a -preset they reject. Data safety: paths are compared case-sensitively off Windows so replace-in-place cannot overwrite an unrelated same-name file, and sibling/separate-directory outputs are written crash-safely. Rules and library: a half-configured rule no longer matches the whole library, files with no audio or an empty-container profile are no longer re-transcoded every sweep, embedded cover art is no longer mistaken for the video stream, and the sweep survives a bad item. Queue: pausing can no longer leave an encode permanently frozen, a just-started job's cancel is no longer lost, and ffmpeg is killed on cancel or shutdown; the encoder-preset cache is now thread-safe and a large library import no longer does O(n^2) work. Also: tighter Dolby Vision detection and UTF-8 decoding of ffmpeg output.

Fixes TV episodes appearing twice in Jellyfin when using the "add as alternate version" output mode. The transcode is linked to its source as an alternate version via a Jellyfin database link, but the plugin fired one merge per completed episode and forced a full library scan each time; those scans re-indexed the freshly-written file concurrently with the merge, and with no locking it was last-writer-wins, so some episodes collapsed to one entry and others were left as a duplicate. Merges are now serialized and no longer force a scan, and the link is applied to the canonical item. Note: Jellyfin's filename version grouping is movies-only, so TV relies on this link; if a duplicate remains, merge the two entries once from the dashboard or use replace-in-place.

Reliability, safety and performance release. Stops the same episode being queued and transcoded more than once (the duplicate "... (1)" outputs). Pausing the queue now also pauses the running encode and resumes it where it left off. Replace-in-place is crash-safe across Docker mounts and never overwrites an unrelated file. "copy" video profiles no longer re-transcode forever; compliance and rules now consider every audio track, not just the first. Removing or cancelling a running job now actually stops its ffmpeg. Security hardening for ffprobe/ffmpeg arguments and input protocols. Performance: ffprobe results are cached so unchanged files are not re-probed every sweep, and the sweep no longer scales with the square of the library size.

Fixes mp4 sources failing within seconds of starting whenever the output container is Matroska. Subtitles in an mp4 are mov_text, which Matroska cannot store, so copying them made the muxer reject the output header and abort the whole transcode (ffmpeg exit code 218, "Function not implemented"). Subtitle tracks are now handled individually: those the output container can store are copied verbatim, and the rest are converted to a text format it can (srt, or WebVTT for webm). mp4 sources therefore transcode successfully and keep their subtitles instead of losing them. Failed jobs on the queue page now expose the ffmpeg output that caused the failure.

Fixes the automatic library sweep re-transcoding files it had already produced output for. In the separate-directory and add-as-alternate-version modes the original source is left unchanged, so every daily sweep re-queued and re-encoded the same files, piling up duplicate outputs. A source is now skipped when the profile's expected output already exists on disk (robust — this survives clearing the job queue) or the queue records a completed transcode for it, and a source that keeps failing is no longer auto-retried after 3 attempts (it can still be requeued manually).

Settings page redesign for clarity: the profile editor is grouped into labelled Video / Resolution / Audio / HDR / Output sections, fields that don't apply are hidden (e.g. CRF only in constant-quality mode, the alternate-version label only for that output mode), every field carries an inline explanation, and advanced ffmpeg arguments are tucked into a collapsed section. The encoder preset is now a real dropdown when ffmpeg enumerates presets (e.g. libx264/x265), falling back to a free-text field with suggestions otherwise. The Queue & status page gains a "Cancel all" button that stops every pending and processing job at once.

Preserves every audio track (all languages) on transcode: a track already in the target codec is copied losslessly, the rest are re-encoded, and each is downmixed only if it individually exceeds the channel cap. For Matroska (mkv) outputs, all subtitle tracks and embedded fonts (for ASS/SSA) are carried across as well. Fixes resolution presets and trigger rules multiplying on every server start/update (constructor-seeded defaults were appended to, rather than replacing, the saved configuration on each load); pre-existing duplicates are now cleaned up automatically on load. Newly-added items still being copied or downloaded are now deferred and re-checked until the file settles, so "queue new items automatically" fires shortly after a file lands instead of waiting for the daily sweep. The "Add as alternate version" output mode now registers the transcoded copy as a proper Jellyfin alternate version (a Merge-Versions database link, source kept as primary) instead of only placing a companion file, so the original and the transcode appear as one movie with a version selector without renaming the original.

Adds a "Scan library now" button (plugin page and queue page) so a sweep can be triggered on demand instead of waiting for the schedule; puts the queue/status page in the dashboard sidebar as its own entry; and shows elapsed time plus an estimated time remaining for running jobs (and total duration for finished ones). Sweeps are now guarded so the scheduled task, the post-scan hook and the button can never overlap.

The "add as alternate version" output mode now uses a configurable version label. Output is named "<original> - <label>.<ext>", which is Jellyfin's native naming convention for alternate versions, so your label (e.g. "H.264 1080p") is what appears in Jellyfin's version selector instead of a hardcoded "pretranscode".

Initial release: dynamic ffmpeg-driven configuration, rules engine, per-library overrides, persistent job queue + verifying worker, library-scan hook, item-added monitor and a daily sweep scheduled task.

versions.changelog:
COMPATIBILITY: Plugin now targets Jellyfin 12.1 (was 10.11.8)
CHANGE: Target framework updated to .NET 10.0 (Jellyfin 12.x requirement)

NEW: NowPlaying JSON now includes itemId (Jellyfin's unique audio item ID) for direct database lookups
CHANGE: itemId is placed right after isPlaying in the JSON response

CRITICAL FIX: UTF-8 encoding in Telnet client — file paths with non-ASCII characters (é, ó, ñ, á, í, ú) are now sent correctly to Liquidsoap, fixing ~80% of silently skipped tracks
FIX: LiquidsoapClient.cs now uses UTF-8 encoding for all Telnet communications instead of ASCII (ASCII corrupted accented characters into '?' causing 'Nonexistent file or ill-formed URI' errors)
FIX: Telnet response reading also uses UTF-8 encoding for consistency
NOTE: Recommended radio.liq changes to further reduce latency and track skipping: disable enable_autocue_metadata(), reduce crossfade to 1.5s, add normalize_url=false to http.get

FIX: NowPlaying JSON year field now returned as quoted string (was unquoted integer causing JSON parse errors in external apps)
FIX: Artwork proxy now actually resizes images based on maxWidth parameter using Jellyfin IImageProcessor (was serving original full-size image regardless of maxWidth value)
FIX: Artwork proxy now uses async IImageProcessor.ProcessImage for proper image processing with SkiaSharp backend

CRITICAL FIX: Eliminated duplicate track reports — Jellyfin was reporting the same song 2-3 times (A,A,A,D,E,E,E pattern) while Icecast played correctly
CRITICAL FIX: NowPlaying JSON and Android app now show the correct current track instead of stale data from duplicate on_track callbacks
FIX: TrackChangeController made fully async — removed .GetAwaiter().GetResult() that caused thread pool starvation and request deadlocks
FIX: Duplicate suppression — same track reported within 15 seconds is suppressed (handles Liquidsoap firing on_track multiple times per play)
FIX: Removed backward drift correction — it caused duplicate track sends to Liquidsoap queue, making playlists longer than expected
FIX: Schedule change now takes immediate priority — RefillQueueAsync aborts if schedule changed, preventing old playlist from continuing past its time slot
IMPROVE: GetCurrentlyPlayingIndexAsync replaces VerifyPositionAsync — only detects stuck tracks, no longer modifies _nextTrackToSend counter

CRITICAL FIX: Liquidsoap stuck detection — when Liquidsoap stops advancing (codec error, corrupt file), the plugin no longer spams queue.append every 5 seconds in an infinite drift correction loop
FIX: VerifyPositionAsync now returns current track index to RefillQueueAsync for stuck detection
FIX: RefillQueueAsync pauses queue refill when Liquidsoap is stuck (same track across consecutive checks)
FIX: Automatically resumes normal refill when Liquidsoap advances past the stuck track
FIX: ResetState clears stuck state (_isStuck, _lastKnownCurrentIdx)

FIX: Tracks silently dropped by Liquidsoap (codec issues, corrupt files) no longer cause premature playlist end — plugin now detects position drift every 5 seconds
FIX: Position verification compares Liquidsoap reality (current_track + queue.length) vs plugin counter to detect skipped tracks
FIX: Playlist now loops automatically when all tracks exhausted but schedule is still active — prevents dead air
IMPROVE: VerifyPositionAsync runs as part of RefillQueueAsync cycle — minimal overhead (one extra Telnet query)
IMPROVE: Detailed warning log when tracks are skipped with exact count of dropped tracks

FIX: NowPlaying endpoint now returns isPlaying=false when radio stops — was stuck showing last track forever

NEW: No Content-Disposition header — displays inline in browser instead of downloading

FIX: artworkUrl in NowPlaying JSON now points to the proxy endpoint instead of Jellyfin's internal image endpoint

IMPROVE: NowPlayingInfo now stores AlbumId (falls back to ItemId if no album parent found)

NEW: Optional maxWidth parameter (default 720) to control artwork resolution (e.g. ?maxWidth=100 for thumbnails)
NEW: NowPlayingInfo class stores current track data (artist, title, album, year, duration, itemId)

IMPROVE: TrackChange stores metadata even when playback reporting is disabled

NEW: NowPlaying public endpoint at /RadioOnline/NowPlaying — returns current track metadata and album artwork URL as JSON for external apps and websites
NEW: Optional maxWidth parameter (default 720) to control artwork resolution (e.g. ?maxWidth=100 for thumbnails)

FIX: Replaced ResetState() with _nextTrackToSend=0 to only reset the send index without destroying the loaded playlist

FIX: Plugin stuck in Inactivo state after failed queue attempts — _currentScheduleKey was set before verifying tracks sent, causing the plugin to never retry loading the playlist
FIX: _currentScheduleKey now only set on successful queue, cleared on failure so next cycle retries automatically
IMPROVE: Error message now includes 'will retry on next cycle' for clarity

ARCHITECTURE: Push metadata — Liquidsoap now TELLS the plugin what's playing via HTTP POST, eliminating all sync issues
NEW: TrackChangeController — HTTP endpoint at /RadioOnline/TrackChange receives track notifications from Liquidsoap
REMOVE: All sync code eliminated — _currentTrackIndex, VerifyTrackSyncAsync, TryResumeCurrentPlaylistAsync, OnReconnected, queue.remaining

SIMPLIFY: LiquidsoapClient — removed OnReconnected event, HadPreviousConnection, GetQueueRemainingAsync

FIX: _currentTrackIndex desync eliminated on restart - Liquidsoap keeps playing uninterrupted while the plugin repositions its tracking to match

name: Transcode Downloader [✓✓]
description:
Adds a quality-selection download button to Jellyfin item detail pages.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 19:22 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ph15ch/Jellyfin-Transcode-Downloader/main/repo/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/ph15ch/Jellyfin-Transcode-Downloader
overview: Adds a 'Download (Transcode…)' entry to the More menu on every movie and episode detail page. Selecting it opens a quality picker — choose a bitrate tier and Jellyfin re-encodes the video server-side to H.264/AAC, streaming it to your browser with a live progress bar, or pick Original to save the unmodified source file directly. Requires the File Transformation companion plugin (>= v2.2.1.0) for permission-safe script injection.

versions.changelog:
feat: choose video and audio codec for transcoded downloads

- The quality sheet now offers a video and an audio codec picker, limited to
  what the server actually has enabled
- Downloads started from an episode list target the episode whose menu you
  opened, instead of the season or series the page is showing
- Failed or empty transcodes now report the real HTTP status instead of
  silently producing a broken file
fix: transcoding actually respects selected quality tier.
fix: i18n strings now load in the correct Jellyfin UI language (de, us, es, fr, nl, zh-cn)

Fix queue panel resetting progress bar when new items are added

Incremental DOM updates replace full re-renders so the active download's
progress bar is preserved when a second item joins the queue.

Add multi-download queue

Downloads now enqueue instead of starting immediately. Each queued item has its own cancel button; cancelling removes only that item and the next starts automatically. The bottom-right panel shows all queued items with live progress for the active one. Queue is in-memory only.
Update logo, rename console prefix to [TranscodeDownloader], fix README and manifest

Fix transcode quality tiers and stale item on first page load

- On first load, quality sheet now awaits metadata before building the
  tier list, so only valid bitrates (below source bitrate) are shown
- Quality sheet now re-derives the item ID from the URL at open time,
  preventing downloads targeting the previous movie when navigating
  between items before the hash-change event fires

Replace dropdown button with action sheet menu entry

- Remove injected select+button from the detail page
- Add 'Download (Transcode…)' entry to Jellyfin's native 'Mehr' menu
- Quality selection via a second overlay in Jellyfin's action sheet style
- Fixes reload-required bug; no longer disrupts the detail page layout

fix: show plugin logo in catalog and installed plugin detail page

- Add imageUrl to manifest.json so the catalog displays the logo
- Include logo.png in the release zip for the installed plugin detail page

rename: QuickDownload → Transcode Downloader + add logo and build CI

- Plugin display name is now "Transcode Downloader"
- All internals renamed to Jellyfin.Plugin.TranscodeDownloader
- Controller route changed to /TranscodeDownloader/ClientScript
- Added logo.png
- Added PR build workflow

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.
fix: delay revokeObjectURL to prevent download failure after completion

fix: button appears on first load without page reload

Replace 20x250ms polling retry loop with a MutationObserver that fires
the moment Jellyfin's SPA renders the detail-view container. The old
loop could time out before the SPA finished hydrating, requiring a
manual page reload to see the download button.

fix: use ApiClient.getItem() for metadata fetch to avoid 401

Jellyfin 10.11 rejects api_key query-param auth on the Items endpoint,
causing the dropdown to stay empty. Switch to client.getItem() which
sends the correct Authorization header.

fix: populate dropdown after UI injection to eliminate race condition

The metadata fetch often completed before Jellyfin rendered the detail
container, so populateDropdown() exited early (select === null) without
ever setting currentItem. Clicking Download then silently did nothing.

- Move currentItem assignment before the early return in populateDropdown()
- Re-call populateDropdown() after injecting the UI if data already arrived
- Reset currentItem when navigating to a new item to avoid stale options

fix: strip Accept-Encoding/Content-Encoding to prevent compressed-body corruption

Jellyfin's static file middleware serves index.html pre-compressed when the
client advertises Accept-Encoding. The IStartupFilter middleware was buffering
those compressed bytes and writing them back with Content-Encoding: gzip still
set, causing browsers to report 'cannot decode raw data'.

Fix: remove Accept-Encoding from the request before intercepting so upstream
never activates compression; also strip Content-Encoding from the response.

fix: inject script tag via middleware — button now appears without companion plugins

The script tag is now injected by an ASP.NET Core IStartupFilter that
intercepts index.html responses in Jellyfin's HTTP pipeline. No File
Transformation plugin required, no disk writes, no timing sensitivity.

Also fixes plugin loading error in the admin UI (Plugin constructor now
calls SetAttributes).

fix: call SetAttributes in Plugin constructor so CanUninstall doesn't throw

BasePlugin (non-generic) never calls SetAttributes — only BasePlugin<T> does
in its own constructor. Without it, AssemblyFilePath stays null, and
CanUninstall throws NullReferenceException when GET /Plugins serializes the
plugin list, breaking the admin plugins page on every page load.

Fix: inject IApplicationPaths and call SetAttributes the same way BasePlugin<T>
does, giving Jellyfin a valid assembly path and data folder path.

Serve client script from controller and inject in-memory

- QuickDownloadController serves the embedded plugin.js at GET /QuickDownload/ClientScript (AllowAnonymous) so the web root never needs to be writable
- WebAssetInjector registers an in-memory File Transformation callback instead of patching index.html on disk; survives Jellyfin web updates and is auto-removed on plugin uninstall
- On-disk fallback retained for installs without File Transformation, with a loud actionable log recommending FT >= v2.2.1.0
- Base-path-aware script src for Jellyfin deployments behind a sub-path

versions.changelog:

Requires Jellyfin 12.

Requires Jellyfin 12.

- Your selected voice track stays selected when moving to the next episode, including choices made through Jellyfin's standard version selector.
- On slow connections, the player buffers video ahead of playback and shows buffering progress.
- Improved playback recovery after temporary loading failures.

Requires Jellyfin 10.11.

## What changed

- Added a complete series voice selector that includes translations available through Jellyfin versions and all supported providers, including Kodik-only coverage.
- A selected voice now stays active across episodes: Jellyfin `Next` and autoplay advance in that voice wherever it is available. `Auto` restores normal automatic selection.
- Improved playback recovery for Alloha, CVH, and Kodik streams, including temporary provider failures, expired stream resources, stalls, and quality fallback.
- Added more accurate episode runtimes and earlier intro/outro skip availability when provider metadata is available.
- Made repeated library refreshes substantially faster when titles and generated files are unchanged, while still rechecking provider coverage when needed.
- Improved mixed-provider libraries where one provider has only part of a season or a translation is available from a different provider.
- Added an optional safe cleanup setting for plugin-managed releases removed from a successfully fetched Yummy user list. It is disabled by default.

## Compatibility

- Requires Jellyfin 10.11.x and .NET 9, unchanged from the previous release.
- Existing plugin configuration remains compatible. The old Jellyfin server base URL value is retained for compatibility but is no longer used or shown; generated streams now use Jellyfin's local gateway automatically.

## After updating

name: JellyToneDown [✓]
description:
Jellyfin plays a theme song in the background when you open a series or a movie, and offers no way to turn it down. JellyToneDown adds one. A server-wide default plus optional per-user levels, applied to theme songs and the audio of theme videos and to nothing else. The adjustment is made on the server, so it reaches every client - the web player, Swiftfin, Findroid, the Android TV app, Kodi and Infuse alike - rather than only the ones that happen to expose a volume control. Files in your library are never modified; adjusted copies live in Jellyfin's cache. The plugin does not download, assign, rename or otherwise manage theme music. It only changes how loud it is.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raleighawes0me/JellyToneDown/main/manifest.json

versions.changelog:
- The in-browser slider is now labelled **All themes**, and carries a tooltip saying it applies
  to every title and to your account only. It always worked that way; appearing over a
  particular series just made it look like a per-series control.
- The per-user settings page says the same thing in the same words.
- The slider now stays up for as long as a theme is actually playing, instead of fading after a
  few seconds. Previously, once it had gone there was no way to get it back for the theme
  already playing short of opening a different title. It still fades a few seconds after the
  theme stops, and hovering it keeps it up as before.
- On narrow screens the panel now drops the percentage rather than the "All themes" label, so
  the thing that says what the slider controls survives on a phone.

- The in-browser volume slider no longer needs a writable web client. The script tag is now
  added to `index.html` as the page is served, by middleware, instead of being written into
  the file on disk. That was the one part of the plugin that did not work on a normal package
  install, where the web client is owned by root and Jellyfin runs as its own user - and it
  also means a Jellyfin upgrade can no longer undo it.
- The old on-disk patch is still selectable under **Web client -> How the script gets in**, and
  switching away from it removes anything it previously wrote.
- The config page now reports how many page loads the script has actually been added to, rather
  than only whether it is switched on.
- The catalogue icon is no longer a square that Jellyfin blew up to fill the card.

- Fixed the per-user settings page always reporting an expired session. Jellyfin 12 ships a
  migration that disables legacy authorization, which switches off the `X-Emby-Token` header
  the page was authenticating with. It now uses the standard `Authorization: MediaBrowser`
  scheme.
- Added a plugin icon.
- Per-version release notes: every version used to read "Initial release" in the catalogue.

- Added a per-user settings page at `/JellyToneDown/MySettings`, so users can set their own
  theme volume without dashboard access. (Shipped broken - fixed in 1.0.2.)
- Adjusted copies are now encoded at the lower of the source bitrate and a per-codec ceiling
  rather than always around 190 kbps, so a 128 kbps theme is no longer inflated.
- The encoder settings are part of the cache key, so changing them invalidates the cache by
  itself.
- Fixed the config page status panel printing the same sentence twice.
- Initial release.

overview: Privacy-first personalized recommendations based on local watch history

versions.changelog:
Jellyfin 10.11.9+ compatibility and recommendation-quality fixes
- Fixes MissingMethodException crash on Jellyfin 10.11.9/10.11.10 (#17, fixes #21): all IUserManager.Users call sites now use GetUsers()
- TV series now weighted by most recently watched episode date instead of always 'today' (#19)
- Replaced play-count rewatch boost with recency-driven Recent Watch Emphasis using decay-squared amplification (#20); the RewatchBoost setting becomes RecentWatchBoost (default 1.0)
- Config page numeric fields saved as 0 no longer revert to defaults (#22)
- REQUIRES Jellyfin 10.11.9 or newer

Migrate from .strm files to filesystem symlinks (#13)
- Fixes transcoded playback on Jellyfin 10.11.7+ (GHSA-j2hf-x4q5-47j3)
- Symlinks preserve source extensions; media pipeline treats them as regular files
- Artwork symlinked from source folder (propagates custom posters automatically)
- Trailer discovery delegated to Jellyfin's native scanner
- Removed ImageSyncService and EnableImageSync/SyncBackdrops settings
- WINDOWS: requires Administrator or Developer Mode enabled for symlink creation

Filter recommendations by user library access (#10)
- Items from libraries a user cannot access are excluded from recommendations
- Applies to both personalized and cold-start recommendation paths
- Respects per-user library permissions including disabled libraries

Fix playback freeze when playing from recommendation libraries (#8)
- Never remove virtual library items from event handlers (deferred to next refresh)
- Ignore PlaybackStart/PlaybackProgress events to prevent DB write storms during playback
- Only sync play status on meaningful events (PlaybackFinished, TogglePlayed, etc.)
- Known tradeoff: partially watched items may appear in Continue Watching twice until next refresh

Bug fixes for series recommendations and playback crashes
- Fixed: Partially watched series not included in watch history, causing all users to get identical cold-start recommendations (#7)
- Fixed: Playback from recommendation libraries crashing with database failures (#8)
- Series watch history now detected at episode level instead of requiring all episodes watched
- Virtual library items no longer removed during active playback

Image sync for custom posters and backdrops
- Custom poster images are now preserved in recommendation libraries
- Copies poster.jpg and backdrop.jpg from source items to virtual folders
- Configurable: Enable/disable image sync and backdrop copying
- Fixes issue where user customizations (e.g., French posters) were lost

Decade-based temporal similarity and bug fix
- Recommendations now consider content from similar time periods
- Decade grouping (1980s, 1990s, etc.) replaces continuous year normalization
- Improves temporal relevance alongside genre/actor/director similarity
- Tested with production data: ~12 decades extracted from 970 items
- Observable impact: 24% of movie recommendations changed, 8% of TV
- Fixed: In-progress TV series no longer appear in recommendations

Series filtering fix and play status sync
- Fixed fully watched series appearing in recommendations
- Play status sync from source library when virtual items are scanned
- Rating proximity scoring feature
- Removed NFO file generation (Jellyfin doesn't read NFO for .strm files)
- Reduced debug logging noise

Fix NFO metadata parsing
- Fixed XML encoding (UTF-16 to UTF-8) so Jellyfin reads runtime correctly
- Added cast, directors, and writers to NFO files
- Added fileinfo/streamdetails for video/audio/subtitle stream selectors

NFO metadata and trailer support
- NFO files with full metadata (runtime, ratings, genres, studios, tags)
- Local trailer support via -trailer.strm files
- Movie folder structure for better metadata handling
- Fixed copy buttons on setup page
- Improved documentation

Initial beta release
- Per-user personalized recommendations for movies and TV shows
- Content-based filtering using TF-IDF embeddings
- Virtual library integration for universal client compatibility
- Configurable weighting (favorites, rewatches, recency)
- Abandoned series exclusion
- Daily scheduled updates with manual refresh option
- Complete privacy - all processing local

versions.changelog:
**Drop-down menus in the theme's look, and a title over the poster that
makes way for the hover buttons.** Jellyfin's drop-down fields - the item
page's audio and subtitle menus, "Add to playlist", the settings - showed
the browser's own grey list; in Chrome and Edge they now take the Dialogs &
menus look and open downwards. With the title printed over the poster, the
watched / favorite / menu buttons were hidden under it and greyed by its
gradient; the title now fades (or slides) away while the pointer is on the
card. All of it is plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and open pages pick it up on their own (a browser holding the old
page in its cache may need one Ctrl+F5).

Drop-down menus

- Dialogs & menus: Jellyfin's drop-down fields take the menus' look - style, color, opacity, blur, corners - with the chosen entry marked in the accent: the item page's version / video / audio / subtitle menus, "Add to playlist" (the one music users meet) and "Add to collection", the user settings for the home screen, playback and subtitles, the metadata editor. They are native selects, and on a computer or a phone the browser drew their list itself, in its own grey, out of any theme's reach. Chrome and Edge (135 and up) now draw it as part of the page (`appearance: base-select`); other browsers keep their own list, in the theme's colors. The TV opens Jellyfin's own menu, which was themed already. Plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.
- The lists open downwards. The browser picks the side with more room, so a field in the lower row of the item page opened upwards; below comes first now, a list that does not fit there gets shorter (it scrolls), and only a field at the very bottom of the window opens upwards.

Cards

- Cards: with the title over the image, the hover buttons (watched, favorite, menu) appeared under it - both sit in the bottom corner, and the title lay on top and took their clicks. The title now makes way while the pointer is on the card: it fades out (the default) or slides down as it fades, and comes back when the pointer leaves. The choice is under the title setting (*Cards → The title when the pointer is on the card*, shown for "Over the image" while the hover buttons are on); "Stays" keeps it as before. Only where the buttons appear - not on the TV or a phone, not on series, seasons and collections whose buttons are hidden, and not on the Seerr rows' cards (their button sits in the middle). Plain CSS, so it works with "CSS only" too.
- Fixed: with the title over the image the hover buttons and the bottom card badges were grey and dull - the dark gradient under the title was painted over them (the same layer, and last in the card). It lies under them now, and while the title makes way the gradient goes with it; Jellyfin's own veil over a hovered card stays.

**A theme applied shows at once, the music player follows the theme, and
"CSS only" is CSS only everywhere.** Jellyfin's client held the branding
CSS for a minute, so open pages kept the old theme after an Apply; the
client script now swaps in the fresh one - on the next navigation within a
second, on a page left open within ten. The music player takes the Player
section's look - until now its bar and sliders stayed in Jellyfin's grey
and blue whatever the theme said. Applied, "CSS only" takes the admin look
off the plugin page at once, the CSS it writes holds nothing for the admin
pages, and a theme exported in that mode is a CSS theme, so an import gives
the same look. Plus a fix for the Sidebar layout, which broke the admin
pages when they followed the defaults.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

A theme applied reaches open pages at once

- Fixed: a theme just applied took a minute or more to show on the user-facing pages - on the admin pages it was there at once. Jellyfin's client keeps the branding CSS it fetched for a minute before it asks again (and a tab left open did not ask until something nudged it). The theme block now carries a stamp, a new `/Jellycanvas/CssStamp` tells the current one in a few bytes, and the client script asks for it when a page loads, on every navigation, when the window or the tab comes back, and every ten seconds while the page is in view; it also watches the client's copy, which the client renders again after a navigation. An older copy is switched off and the fresh CSS goes in over it until the client catches up - a navigation shows the new theme within a second, a page just left open within ten. With "CSS only" there is no script, and Jellyfin's minute stays.
- The client script runs for an applied theme even without a feature of its own (that check is its job then).
- The startup refresh compares the stamp: the date line in the block made it rewrite Branding on every start, even with nothing changed.

The music player

- The music player follows the Player section: its bar along the bottom takes the control bar's style (solid, glass, gradient and the rest, its color, opacity, blur), floats and rounds like it, and its buttons take the buttons' size. The position and volume sliders - in the bar and on the queue page - take the progress slider's color and the position ones its height. Until now all of it stayed in Jellyfin's stock grey and hard-coded blue.
- Sliders anywhere else (a settings page, say) take the accent instead of Jellyfin blue.
- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout the music bar ran under the sidebar and covered its bottom (the user button among it); it starts where the content does now.
- Test server: `test\Make-Music.ps1` adds a music library - three made-up albums of generated tones, tagged and with covers - to check the music pages against a theme.

CSS only

- Fixed: after "CSS only" was applied, the plugin page itself - an admin page - kept the custom Dashboard look until it was reloaded. The client script running in it went on with what it had fetched when the page loaded. The designer now swaps it for what the server serves after every Apply and every Remove: nothing after CSS only (the admin pages turn stock at once), and the fresh admin look after an ordinary Apply, which until now also waited for a reload.
- CSS only: the theme no longer writes its rules for the admin pages - without the script they never reach them (Jellyfin renders Branding on the user-facing pages only), so they were dead weight.
- Share: a theme exported in "CSS only" mode carries the CSS look only. The script's features were hidden from its author, yet the export took whatever they still held (from before the switch, or from an import) - so an import brought a slideshow, badges or an admin look nobody had seen with that theme. The admin pages are left out now (their panel settings, "Theme the Dashboard" and the Dashboard tab's document), and of the script's features only their switches go along, turned off (the slideshow, the badges, the item page's banner, the info bar's close button) - an import gives the same CSS version, and the theme site no longer lists such a theme as needing File Transformation or styling the admin pages. The importer's own "CSS only" choice, buttons and Seerr stay theirs, as before. The Share section says so while CSS only is on.
- Designer: unticking "CSS only" brings the script features back into the preview straight away; until now they came back only with the next change to a script setting.

The admin pages

- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout and the theme on the Dashboard, the admin pages fell apart - their top bar was turned into the sidebar column and went off the screen, and the content slid under the admin menu. The admin pages have a menu of their own on the left, so the sidebar now stays on the user-facing pages and the admin bar docks next to the menu as before. The Dashboard tab no longer offers a layout either; it shows the bar's own settings.

The designer

- Designer: rows show where they do something - the "Play" label only while the other buttons have no labels (with labels on, Play has one anyway), the logo's height for the Jellyfin icon or a custom image and its width for a custom image only, and the info bar's settings only while the bar is on.

**The loading ring gets a look of its own, and a season's episodes get
their badges.** The ring Jellyfin shows while a stream starts can take one
of six styles, a color, size, speed, a glow and a disc behind it - and even
left alone it now follows the theme's accent instead of Jellyfin blue. The
episodes on a season's page carry the card badges, the home slideshow's
button picks its icon from a list, and the Dashboard's device cards lose
the dark boxes a lighter now-playing veil left behind their text.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

The player

- Player: the loading ring - the one Jellyfin shows while a stream starts (and, being the same element, while a page loads) - has settings of its own (Player -> Loading ring): Jellyfin's ring, a ring, a double ring, an orbiting dot, a pulse or three dots; its color (empty = the accent), size, line thickness and speed; a glow in its color; and a dark or frosted disc behind it. The player preview shows it in the middle, and Ctrl+click on it opens these settings. Jellyfin paints its ring blue by hard-coded value, so even untouched it now takes the theme's accent.

Home slideshow

- Home slideshow: the button's icon is picked from a list - info, play, play in a circle, a screen with play, arrows, open, eye, film strip, cinema, compass, star, heart, three dots, or none - with the chosen icon shown next to the label. "Another one" brings back the name field for any Material icon, and a theme with an icon outside the list opens with that field.
- Fixed: the home slideshow's button style did nothing in the designer's preview - the button kept the look it had when the slideshow first appeared. The slideshow writes its own stylesheet, and when the script started again with new settings (the preview restarts it on every change) it found the old sheet and left it alone. A real client loads the page afresh, so the applied style was right there. The sheet is rewritten now, and it goes with the rest of the script's leftovers when the script stops.

The admin pages

- Fixed: on the Dashboard, a device card with nothing playing showed dark boxes behind its lines of text as soon as "Darkening over a playing session's picture" was changed. The darkening went on every stack inside the card - and an idle card is built of several, one per line - instead of the one that covers a playing card's picture; it now goes only there, and only on a card that has a picture.
- Dashboard: the text on a device card without a picture follows the card's color - the theme's text where it reads well on it (4.5 : 1), otherwise white or near-black, whichever stands out more. The card is the accent laid over the panel; a light accent no longer leaves white text on yellow.

Card badges

Security and speed

- Security: the random background picks only items every enabled account may see. Its address is anonymous (the login page uses it, and a CSS `url()` cannot carry a token), so it cannot tell who is looking - and until now it could put a backdrop from a library a child's account is kept out of, or one rated above that account's limit, on the login page or behind that child's home screen. Library access, the parental rating and blocked tags of every account are respected now.
- Security: text the theme writes into a CSS string (the `content:` of a label) loses every control character, not just line breaks - a form feed also ends a CSS string and would let the rest of the text be read as rules.
- Security: the settings baked into the client script escape `<`, `>`, `&` and `'` (before, only `</` was defused), so the script stays whole even when pasted inline into an HTML page by an injector plugin. Letters of every language stay readable.
- Faster: "Slow panning animation" moves the picture's layer instead of the picture inside it. It animated `background-position`, which makes the browser restyle and repaint a full-screen picture every frame; a `transform` runs on the compositor. A home page at rest with a panning random background went from about 120 ms of main-thread work per 8 seconds to 16 ms (Chrome, desktop) - on a weak TV it was most of what the page cost. It looks the same, portrait phones included.
- Seerr posters: the disk cache no longer grows for ever - posters nobody asked for in 30 days go (checked at most once a day). A poster is written aside and moved in whole, so two requests at once never read a half-written file; after a server restart a poster already on disk is served straight away instead of a 404 until Seerr has answered again; a download is capped at 4 MB.
